In author-run evaluations, split-sample partition selection gains a reported mean 0.060 coverage over support balancing, with a positive direction in 59 of 60 model effects across three intent-routing datasets and two architectures; a naive estimator captures only 0.005 of a reported 0.157 population-known opportunity.
items.title: Available Guardrails quantifies when selective prediction can be certified

items.content_text: The September 2026 RegimeAbstain preprint models retrieval confidence from query and approximate-nearest-neighbor structure, without an extra language-model call, then abstains on risky multi-hop retrievals. Across three benchmarks and two retrieval architectures, the authors report confident-wrong-answer rates of 14.5%–62.1%. On MuSiQue with an LLM-judge pipeline, they report reducing that rate from 39.5% to 20.6% at 50% coverage, with expected calibration error 0.035.
items.title: RegimeAbstain estimates multi-hop retrieval failure from query and ANN structure

items.content_text: The September 2026 AutoViewMem preprint proposes learning low-overlap semantic views from conversational traces and using them to structure memory at write time, followed by offline consolidation and ordinary top-K retrieval. The authors report improved long-horizon question answering and personalization over memory baselines on LoCoMo and PersonaMem with Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B.
items.title: AutoViewMem organizes long-term conversational memory into learned semantic views

items.content_text: A September 18, 2026 arXiv preprint introduces a benchmark for continual world models in robot manipulation. Six simulated task curricula end with compositions of earlier action and perception primitives, separating reuse on a new task from forgetting on earlier tasks. The authors evaluate DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 with fine-tuning, replay, EWC and PackNet, plus a modular Prismatic World Model. In a diagnostic with an encoder pretrained on demonstrations from all benchmark tasks and then frozen, PWM reports mean forgetting score 3.85 and forward-transfer score 36.18 across six suites, compared with 34.97 and 38.11 for TD-MPC2 using that same encoder; lower forgetting and higher forward transfer are better. Without this privileged encoder, PWM is reported on par with TD-MPC2. The study is limited to simulation, three seeds, selected model settings, and no controlled parameter or compute budgets; it does not establish physical-robot performance.
items.title: A compositional benchmark exposes the reuse–forgetting tradeoff in continual robot world models

items.content_text: A September 18, 2026 arXiv preprint describes Touvigation, a phone-based assistive object-acquisition system that combines vision-language interpretation with persistent local 3D tracking. Its audio guidance shifts from room-scale orientation and step counts to body-relative reaching cues and tactile verification. In a within-subject study, the authors report 48 successful trials out of 48 with Touvigation, versus 28/48 with ByteDance's Doubao assistant and 41/48 without AI; they also report faster completion and lower workload. The finding is bounded to 12 blind adults, two unfamiliar rooms and short-term use after familiarization. Participants were from one regional community and one severity category; the system depends on a LiDAR-equipped chest-mounted iPhone, initial room scanning, stable tracking and cloud processing. The study has not been independently replicated.
tags: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
items.title: A preprint reports that persistent spatial guidance improved object acquisition in a small blind-user study

items.content_text: On September 17, 2026, Australia’s Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet opened a consultation on proposed national standards for large data centres and conditions for frontier AI training. The paper links the policy design to attracting investment while managing energy, water, community and workforce effects; it also says copyright treatment, creator protections, local research capability and compute access matter to AI training policy. The consultation asks how the government should secure local contributions and protect creators while providing regulatory certainty. It does not announce a final policy, create a copyright exception or document a company-specific bargain. Submissions closed October 9, 2026, and the paper says responses and stakeholder engagement will inform later standards.
tags: Australian Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet
items.title: Australia consults on conditions for AI training, creator rights and infrastructure investment

items.content_text: A September 21, 2026 arXiv preprint proposes TTSE, which evolves environmental facts (FACT) separately from task-conditioned procedures (TIP), using interaction evidence to revise or retire both kinds of rule. The paper frames representation errors and execution errors as distinct contributors to agent failure and evaluates the framework on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, GDPevo, SOPBench and PinchBench. Authors report gains over selected baselines and an end-to-end PinchBench score of 0.7822 versus 0.7439 across three runs. In the SOPBench comparison, the reported dual-track gain over a single-track Bayesian-memory ablation is 2.99 percentage points over 892 tasks, but warehouse inspection contributes 78% of the gain; without that domain the reported gap is 0.67 points, and dangerous-goods tasks slightly favor single-track. The preprint reports no independent reproduction; its GDPevo dual-versus-TIP ablation is not formally significance-tested, and induced rules lack a structured verification gate.
items.title: A preprint reports that separating environmental facts from task procedures can help evolving agents

items.content_text: A September 21, 2026 arXiv preprint evaluates a model's sensitivity to question-relevant image crops as a label-free visual-evidence signal. On one 191-example V*Bench evaluation using three Qwen vision-language models, the authors report that selecting among 16 candidate crops raised fine-grained answer accuracy from about 70% to 85% and localized target regions 4.4–5.1 times above chance. Combining the evidence-gap signal with model confidence improved correctness prediction in the reported test. The authors also tested gated self-distillation: on HR-Bench, no gating, trajectory gating and token gating all scored below the base model, with more aggressive gating performing worse. The inference and training findings come from different tests and should remain separate. Results are author-reported, unreproduced and limited to one small benchmark; the crop search also requires 16 forward passes per example.
items.title: A preprint reports label-free visual grounding gains at inference, but not from pilot distillation

items.content_text: A September 21, 2026 arXiv preprint reports an evaluation of GPT-6 Astra acting directly as a robot manipulation policy, without task-specific fine-tuning or a learned motor policy in the control path. Across 42 RoboDojo simulation tasks and 2,100 trials, the authors report 22.48% average success and a score of 28.97, above the 40 public policies in their September 10 leaderboard snapshot. The result is uneven: Astra trails the top policy on precision, long-horizon and memory axes, while GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-Flash perform much worse in the same reported interface. The authors say they stopped real-robot trials after unsafe actions damaged equipment; the paper does not establish real-world reliability or safe control. These are preprint-reported results without independent reproduction, and the public-policy runs did not receive the wiki-derived task text supplied to the LLMs.
items.title: A preprint reports GPT-6 Astra leading a simulated robot benchmark, with sharp control limits

items.content_text: A September 20 preprint introduces BabelFlow, a workflow for adapting agent benchmarks across languages while preserving links among prompts, tools, environments and evaluators, and releases BabelArena with 16,146 instances across 23 languages. In a 40-task Chinese ablation, the authors report fewer broken references and behavioral mismatches than independent translation, at higher token cost. Their five-model evaluation reports lower task success and language consistency in the low-resource language group, with distinct tool-use/control-flow failures and increased input-token use in sampled tasks. These are paper-reported findings; translation validity, independent reproduction and generalization remain open.
items.title: BabelArena tests agent execution across 23 languages and reports resource-linked failure gaps

items.content_text: An October 8 v3 preprint introduces MemCalib, a benchmark that scores whether each fact in an agent’s stored memory should be ignored, used as bounded support, or allowed to control the answer. The authors report 15,000 examples across health, general assistance and coding. On its 1,500-example test set, the highest listed exact calibration is 28.40% for GPT-5.6-SOL; most evaluated models more often over-use memory than under-use it. The authors report that MemCalib-RL improves Qwen3-8B atom-use accuracy on this benchmark and transfers to a 150-query RPEval subset, while increasing under-use relative to the base model. Results are paper-reported and rely on constructed memory examples and rubric-guided model judging; real-world transfer is unknown.
items.title: MemCalib measures whether language-model agents give stored facts the right influence

items.content_text: A September 2026 preprint defines Loopjacking as product logic applying a human decision for an operation A to a materially different operation B. In purposively selected tests, the author reports post-approval substitution in seven sampled Agno AgentOS releases and 12 sampled in-memory LangGraph Agent Server compositions with a declared authorization policy, plus an incomplete shell-command approval representation in OpenClaw 2026.2.23. OpenClaw 2026.2.24 rejected the tested mismatch. OpenAI Agents SDK 0.22.0 and 0.22.2 served as negative controls that rejected same-call mutation. The tests used synthetic principals and harmless recording sinks; they do not estimate prevalence, establish user susceptibility, or show all versions are affected.
items.title: Loopjacking paper reports agent approval reused for materially changed operations in tested product paths

items.content_text: Cisco's September 21, 2026 report describes an MLPerf Inference v6.1 GPT-OSS 120B Server submission that split prefill across eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs and decode across eight AMD Instinct MI350X GPUs over a Cisco Ethernet fabric. Cisco reports 70,085.48 tokens/s as the arithmetic sum of separately measured system throughputs and 73,357.62 tokens/s when combined (104.7% of that sum), while meeting applicable p99 TTFT and TPOT limits. MLCommons separately identifies Cisco as the first cross-vendor heterogeneous accelerator submission. The accessible MLCommons summary does not repeat Cisco's exact throughput figures, and the official raw workbook was not retrievable in this review; the numeric performance comparison therefore remains attributed to Cisco.
items.title: Cisco reports cross-vendor H200/MI350X inference above standalone throughput sum

items.content_text: A September 2026 preprint introduces INSPECT, which learns robot view preferences from egocentric assembly-assistant records by separating evidence needed to resolve a claim from observation changes a robot camera can reproduce, then calibrating relative views to robot pose. In offline fixed-lattice replay on gearbox assemblies, the authors report mean human-rated view utility of 1.205 and full verifiability of 41.7% across 132 matched trials, versus 1.045 and 34.8% for the current-view baseline. On 1,068 IMPACT trials, its relative-view selector reports a 54.3% correct-decision rate versus 50.6% for current view. These are author-reported results in two constrained replay settings, not a live closed-loop deployment or independent reproduction.
items.title: INSPECT learns robot inspection views from assembly-assistant records

items.content_text: In a September 25, 2026 Chinese-language company report about its 2026 Cloud栖 Conference, Alibaba said Qwen 4 was in training and gave a roadmap for Qwen 4.5 and Qwen 5 to scale to 5–10 trillion parameters. It described its Zhenwu V900 accelerator as up to three times the performance of M890, with 216 GB memory and 1,200 GB/s interconnect bandwidth, and said mass production and market launch were planned for 2027 Q1. Alibaba also set a target for Alibaba Cloud-operated global data-center capacity to exceed 20 GW by 2032. These are company-reported plans and specifications; independent model, chip-performance and capacity evidence was not inspected.
items.title: Alibaba announces 5–10T Qwen roadmap, V900 accelerator and 2032 cloud-capacity target

items.content_text: On September 21, 2026, the California Governor's Office announced the signing of seven bills addressing data-center electricity, water, reporting, environmental review and rate structures. Its summary says the package will require water and electricity reporting, place specified grid-upgrade costs on data centers, require proposed projects to provide water information to local governments and suppliers, and narrow blanket environmental exemptions. These provisions are described from the Governor's announcement; the chaptered statutes were not accessible in this review, so exact covered facilities, duties, exemptions, effective dates and implementation are not independently stated here.
items.title: California signs seven data-center bills covering utility costs, reporting, water and siting
